item.title: Eigenspaces of Preserved Graph Laplacian Eigenvalues under Positive Edge-Weight Addition
item.description: arXiv:2610.14310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how the eigenspace associated with a fixed graph Laplacian eigenvalue changes under positive edge updates, allowing both new edges and increases in existing edge weights. We show that a preserved eigenvalue may have inherited eigenvectors from the original eigenspace and emergent eigenvectors outside it. We characterize the inherited eigenspace and show that it is independent of the update weights. We characterize its orthogonal complement within the preserved eigenspace through a symmetric matrix whose size is at most the number of updated edges, yielding a multiplicity formula and an explicit reconstruction of the updated eigenspace. For fixed updated edges, we characterize when emergence is possible and show that, whenever it is, equal update weights suffice. The exceptional weights form the zero set of a nonzero multi-affine polynomial in reciprocal variables and have Lebesgue measure zero. Finally, emergence cannot occur at either of the two smallest Laplacian eigenvalues, counting multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: Maribel Bueno, Susana Furtado, Javier P\'erez

item.title: A note on Guo's perturbation result for symmetric nonnegative matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.14759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1997 Guo Wuwen proved that if $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix with Perron eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ real, then $(\lambda_1+t,\lambda_2\pm t,\lambda_3,\dots,\lambda_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix for every $t\ge 0$. Whether the same holds for symmetric nonnegative matrices has remained an open question. We give an affirmative answer, in a slightly stronger form: if $A$ is a symmetric nonnegative matrix with eigenvalues $\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$ and $d_1\ge|d_2|+\dots+|d_n|$, then there is a symmetric matrix $B\ge A$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_1+d_1,\dots,\lambda_n+d_n$, and $B$ has the same diagonal as $A$ when $d_1+\dots+d_n=0$. This leads us to call a symmetrically realizable list Guo-extreme if none of Guo's moves can be reversed within the set of symmetrically realizable lists. Every symmetrically realizable list is a Guo-extreme list plus a vector from the cone of Guo's moves. Our second main result is a certificate, modelled on a theorem of Laffey on extreme symmetric matrices: if $A$ is irreducible and every nonnegative symmetric matrix that commutes with $A$ and vanishes wherever $A$ is positive is a multiple of the identity, then the spectrum of $A$ can be moved by a small amount in every trace-preserving direction (in every direction, if $A$ has a positive diagonal entry) and remain symmetrically realizable; in particular it is not Guo-extreme.
item.dc:creator: Helena \v{S}migoc

item.title: An optimization problem for $\delta'$ leaky stars
item.description: arXiv:2610.15771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider singular Schr\"odinger operators with an attractive $\delta'$ interaction of strength $\beta$ supported by a star graph and prove that the ground-state eigenvalue is uniquely maximized by stars of the maximum symmetry. Two different proofs are presented, one for an even number of edges using a comparison to the $\delta$ interaction star, the other general based on Birman-Schwinger technique.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Exner

item.title: Semigroup properties of Schr\"{o}dinger operators with complex singular potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.16670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the complex Hilbert space $L_2(\mathbb{R}_+)$ on the half-line $\mathbb{R}_+ = [0, \infty)$, we investigate non-symmetric Schr\"odinger operators \[ Su = -u'' + qu, \qquad u(0) = 0, \] with complex-valued, highly singular distributional potentials \[ q = s + Q' \in H_{\mathrm{loc}}^{-1}(\mathbb{R}_+), \qquad s \in L_{1,\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}_+), \quad Q \in L_{2,\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}_+), \] where the derivative $Q'$ is understood in the sense of Schwartz distributions. A rigorous operator-theoretic setting is established within the framework of Shin--Zettl quasi-derivatives. We prove that every accretive operator $S$ of this class is automatically $m$-accretive in $L_2(\mathbb{R}_+)$ and $C$-self-adjoint with respect to the complex conjugation involution $C : u \mapsto \bar{u}$. In particular, no additional boundary conditions at infinity are needed, meaning that a Weyl limit-point type situation always prevails for accretive realizations. Constructive local conditions on the coefficients $s$ and $Q$ are found under which the generated strongly continuous semigroup $\{e^{-tS}\}_{t \ge 0}$ is contractive or holomorphic in a sector of the complex plane.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Mikhailets, Volodymyr Molyboga

item.title: The Adiabatic b-Calculus and the Global Anomaly Formula on Manifolds with Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.16938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the determinant line bundle for a family of elliptic operators on compact manifolds with boundary with the associated Quillen metric and Bismut-Freed connection, and we prove the global anomaly formula in this context. This extends Witten's holonomy theorem to manifolds with boundary. Witten studied the limiting behavior of the eta invariant of a Dirac operator on the total space of a fibration over $\mathbb{S}^1$ when the metric in the base $\mathbb{S}^1$ is blown up in a certain manner, a process known as taking the adiabatic limit. In this paper, we construct the calculus of adiabatic $b$-pseudodifferential operators, which naturally synthesizes the $b$-calculus and the adiabatic calculus of pseudodifferential operators. Using this calculus, and assuming the fiber operators to be invertible, we compute the adiabatic limit of the natural eta invariant in this setting and relate it to the integral of the Bismut-Freed connection and new correction terms coming from the boundary of the fibers.
item.dc:creator: Chad Nelson

item.title: (Sharp arithmetic) localization beyond transversality
item.description: arXiv:2610.17139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sharp arithmetic localization for one-dimensional quasiperiodic potentials with jump discontinuities, beyond uniform transversality. Our results include every non-constant $C^1$ monotone sampling function, even with arbitrarily large flat regions, and also certain non-monotone potentials. A key new mechanism is a symbolic unique-continuation principle: first-return words to the region where $f'>0$ have no common Dirichlet resonance, forcing eigenfunction mass to transfer away from flat or negatively sloped regions and recovering quantitative monotonicity of finite-volume eigenvalue branches.
item.dc:creator: Svetlana Jitomirskaya, Netanel Levi, Tom Stoiber

item.title: Resonance counting and spectral gaps for hyperbolic surfaces via Fourier decay
item.description: arXiv:2610.17276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an improved fractal Weyl upper bound for resonances of infinite-area convex cocompact hyperbolic surfaces, expressed in terms of the Hausdorff dimension of the limit set and the Fourier decay exponent of the Patterson--Sullivan measure. This bound also yields a sharper upper bound for the essential spectral gap for these surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Louis Soares

item.title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problem for the Schr\"odinger Operator on a Compact Graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.18081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for the first $m$ eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator on a compact metric graph. We prove the existence of a solution for every strictly increasing finite set of prescribed eigenvalues. On a graph without cycles, we obtain a representation of the optimal correction as a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions, provided that the selected eigenvalues are simple and separated from the next eigenvalue. On a graph with cycles, under the same simplicity and separation assumptions, we obtain a strong limiting representation of the optimal potential in terms of eigenfunctions of approximating operators. For a graph with a cycle, we give a counterexample with simple eigenvalues and linearly dependent squared eigenfunctions. We also prove that linear dependence of the squares of nonzero restrictions to an edge of eigenfunctions corresponding to distinct eigenvalues forces the potential on that edge to have an analytic representative
item.dc:creator: Valeev Nur

item.title: Square-Root Profiles and Sharp Fourier Decay of Quasiperiodic Spectral Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.18259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study spectral measures of one-dimensional quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators. For subcritical Schr\"odinger operator with Diophantine frequency, we prove sharp measurable-set bounds, answering a question of Avila and Jitomirskaya \cite{AJ}; we prove optimal Fourier decay and the sharp decay order of the time-averaged quantum return probability, confirming a conjecture of Aloisio, Carvalho, and de Oliveira \cite{ACO} and a prediction of Zhong and Mosseri \cite{ZhongMosseri}. For the subcritical almost Mathieu operator, we establish summable square-root envelopes for the spectral density, with an optimal density-one formulation of the lower bound, thereby answering a question of Avila \cite{Aqi}. These results follow from a general theorem for reflectionless measures under a summable square-root Craig-type condition. We establish an exact residue expansion of the squared Borel transform, which connects local density blow-up with long-time averaged return probabilities: the endpoint residues determine both the square-root edge profiles and the leading coefficient of the time-averaged return probability.
item.dc:creator: Zhenfu Wang, Qi Zhou

item.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: Counterexamples to the 2005 polygon conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.14100v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $\Lambda_n=S_n$. We observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, which gives a short proof of $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$, and we describe $\Lambda_n$ as a union, over all vectors $v$, of intersections of zonotopes $Z_i(v)$ built from the ratios $v_j/v_i$. For a vector whose components are the $n$ distinct $n$th roots of unity, every $Z_i(v)$ equals $S_n$. We then show that the conjecture is false for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with one vertex duplicated has an eigenvalue lying $2.1\cdot10^{-4}$ beyond one edge of $S_7$. For the analogous digraph of order $n$, the corresponding eigenvalue lies at signed distance $\delta_n\sim\frac{\pi^2}{2n^4}$ beyond the supporting line of the analogous edge of $S_n$, so the construction yields counterexamples for all sufficiently large $n$; numerically, it does so for every $7\le n\le300$. We also prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$, with $S_m\setminus\{0,1\}$ lying in the interior of $S_n$ for $n\ge3m$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Chebotarev

item.title: Continuous meets discrete: geometry dependence of the performance of iterative solutions for nonsymmetric PDEs in terms of Laplace eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2610.14946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is a classical fact in spectral geometry that the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian depend continuously on the geometry of the underlying domain, under suitable geometric restrictions. We show that this theoretical property is reflected in a concrete numerical situation: the convergence rate of iterative solvers for convection-diffusion problems remains stable under deformations of the domain. The connection is a superlinear estimate for preconditioned GMRES/GCR in which the relative residual errors are bounded by an explicit expression of the eigenvalues of the Laplacian, or of a symmetric positive elliptic operator in divergence form. We prove that this bound depends continuously on the domain, uniformly in the iteration index, under either regularity hypotheses on the boundary or a topological constraint in dimension two. We also establish corresponding statements on the discrete level. Two examples delimit the theory: domains bounded by a fractal curve, where continuity still holds, and perforated domains, where it fails. The theoretical results, including both examples with rough domains, are confirmed by numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: F. Francesconi, J. Kar\'atson, B. Lados, J. Rowlett

item.title: Dimensional transition and spectral instability in lattice Hardy inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.14950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discretization can change a sharp stability threshold even when the continuum threshold is recovered at infinity. We study this phenomenon for the Hardy inequality on the integer lattice in dimensions at least three: its best coefficient agrees with the continuum value through dimension eight and is smaller from dimension nine onwards. We characterize this transition by the total critical defect, the summable error obtained by testing the lattice operator against the critical continuum power. A theta-function representation proves that the defect is negative and strictly decreasing from dimension nine; explicit positive Hardy remainders establish its positivity in dimensions three through eight. An exact energy identity relates this defect to the energy saved by optimizing the profile outside the neighbours of the origin. This exterior remains stable in dimensions eight and nine, locating the first loss of positivity in its coupling to those neighbours. We give self-contained proofs of both dimensional ranges. We then describe how local attraction creates a negative eigenvalue in a general class of lattice operators with critical inverse-square tails. Its magnitude is exponentially small near the threshold, with both the rate and the multiplicative prefactor determined by zero-energy solutions. The result allows connected finite modifications of the lattice and nonradial corrections to the tail. The same analysis controls the spread of the emerging state and gives a two-dimensional return scale for the associated Markov chain in every ambient dimension.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Lizama

item.title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16157v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $\lambda$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(\lambda^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\log\lambda)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.
item.dc:creator: Xing Wang, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Optimal information loss for Liouville spectral responses
item.description: arXiv:2610.16321v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Fisher information about the amplitude of a known smooth mean shift from the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and spatial responses of a Liouville random medium. The complete response record determines the speed measure and the Gaussian free field, whereas every finite record strictly loses information; an optimal design exists in each finite-dimensional probe space. We quantify this gap as the known Liouville parameter $\gamma$ tends to zero. If the probe space contains an explicit matching probe, the minimum loss equals $\gamma^2$ times a positive compression error for a deterministic second-chaos operator, up to $o(\gamma^2)$, with designs allowed to depend on $\gamma$. After enlarging the probe dictionary, the optimal $m$-response coefficient is asymptotic to $\|Lg\|_{L^1(D)}^2/(8m)$, where $L=-(2\pi)^{-1}\Delta_D$ on the unit disk $D$. A quadratic correction of the readouts attains the same fixed-design loss to second order.
item.dc:creator: Chunhao Cai

item.title: A geometric lower bound for the clamped plate eigenvalue problem in low dimensions and extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the spectrum of the Dirichlet-biLaplacian can be quantitatively bounded from below in terms of the inradius only, for a general open set in dimensions $2$ and $3$. For the same dimensions, we also extend this result to fractional powers $s$ of the Laplacian, with $N/2<s<2$. The resulting estimate comes with a constant having the correct asymptotic behavior as $s$ approaches the two endpoints $N/2$ and $2$. The proofs exploit capacitary techniques in the vein of Maz'ya.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Bianchi, Francesco Bozzola, Lorenzo Brasco

item.title: Semiclassical Moser--Trudinger type inequalities for orthonormal families in $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.16922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$-orthonormal families $\{u_n\}_{n=1}^N$ with one-body density $\rho=\sum_{n=1}^N |u_n|^2$, we prove the whole-space endpoint Moser--Trudinger inequality $$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\frac{e^{4\pi\rho(x)}-1-4\pi\rho(x)}{\rho(x)}\,dx \le C\left(N-1+\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\rho(x)\,dx\right), $$ where the integrand on the left-hand side is defined to be zero on $\{x: \rho(x)=0\}$. We develop a heat-semigroup refinement of Rumin's density method to treat both the endpoint coefficient $4\pi$ and the whole-space setting. Our inequality is sharp in two respects: the optimality of the coefficient $4\pi$ and the linear growth in the rank $N$. Moreover, through a semiclassical analysis of the density generated by normalized Dirichlet eigenfunctions, we establish the collective asymptotic behaviors of the quantities appearing in the inequality in various regimes. These semiclassical behaviors show that the rank-dependent term $N-1$ on the right-hand side is indispensable.
item.dc:creator: Phuoc-Tai Nguyen, Tuan-Dat Tran

item.title: Spectral and Nodal Properties of Static Manifolds with Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.16974v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study compact static manifolds with boundary from a spectral point of view, with particular emphasis on the relation between Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin spectra and the nodal structure of static potentials. We establish comparison inequalities linking Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues with the scalar curvature and derive sufficient spectral conditions ensuring that a static potential changes sign. We also obtain bounds on the number of connected components of the zero set, sufficient conditions for its connectedness, and sufficient conditions ensuring that its components intersect the boundary. Finally, we study variational properties of Robin static triples and characterize compact Robin static triples whose metrics are critical for the first mixed Robin--Dirichlet eigenvalue under admissible volume-preserving deformations.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Medvedev

item.title: Yau's number-theoretic conjecture and sharp spectral bounds for quantum harmonic oscillators
item.description: arXiv:2610.17704v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Yau's number-theoretic conjecture on positive integral points in real right simplices in every dimension $n\ge3$, and apply the resulting sharp polynomial bound to quantum harmonic oscillators. The lattice-point bound holds for every choice of positive real intercepts for which the count is nonzero, with equality precisely when all intercepts equal the same integer. For oscillators in dimensions $n\ge3$, we obtain explicit upper bounds for eigenvalue counts and spectral remainders for arbitrary positive frequencies at every threshold at or above the lowest eigenvalue. For frequencies with rational ratios in dimensions $n\ge2$, an additional lattice coordinate and interpolation give bounds for energy sums, or first Riesz means, at every threshold. When all frequencies are equal (the isotropic case), the oscillator attains these bounds: the counting bound is exact at its energy levels, and interpolation on its natural energy grid recovers the energy sum at every threshold. In three dimensions, the exact formula displays the periodic contribution associated with the resonance discussed by Fefferman and Seco. The proof builds on the slicing method of Yau and Zhang. Arithmetic and geometric consequences include explicit bounds for smooth numbers and lattice-point discrepancies.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwen Liu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Hao Zuo

item.title: $L^2$ convergence rates for singular stochastic wave dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17815v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish quantitative hypocoercivity for singular stochastic damped wave equations arising in stochastic quantization. Building on the finite-dimensional argument of Cao, Lu, and Wang [Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal. 2023], we derive a dimension-free criterion that replaces uniform semiconvexity by a log-Sobolev inequality together with exponential lower-tail bounds for the bottom of the Hessian spectrum. We verify this criterion for the two-dimensional $\Phi^4_2$ and sine-Gordon models and for the three-dimensional $\Phi^4_3$ model, through estimates on the lowest eigenvalue of associated singular random Schr\"odinger operators. Combined with the continuum limit established in a companion paper, this yields exponential $L^2$ convergence to equilibrium for the $\Phi^4_2$ dynamics and for sine-Gordon with $\beta^2<2\pi$. For $\Phi^4_2$, we verify that in a weak-coupling, small-mass regime, optimizing the damping yields a kinetic relaxation rate of at least order $m$. This yields a genuine acceleration over the order-$m^2$ relaxation rate of the overdamped dynamics. The lattice estimates are uniform in the discretization for sine-Gordon throughout $\beta^2<4\pi$, and for $\Phi^4_3$ at fixed volume, including regimes beyond those for which the continuum dynamics is vpresently constructed.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay Barashkov, Giacomo Di Ges\`u, Petri Laarne

item.title: Eigenvalue fluctuations for the crushed ice problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.18013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the eigenvalues of the negative Dirichlet Laplacian $-\Delta$ in domain $D_{\epsilon,N}$ obtained by removing $N$ Euclidean balls of radius $\epsilon$ from a bounded open set $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ ($d\ge2$). It is known that, for the balls centered at points drawn independently from a distribution with probability density $\rho$ and for $N\to\infty$ and $\epsilon\downarrow0$ so that the aggregate Newtonian capacity of the removed balls tends to some $\kappa>0$, the eigenvalues of $-\Delta$ in $D_{\epsilon,N}$ homogenize to those of the Schr\"odinger operator $-\Delta+\kappa\rho$ in $D$. Here we prove that, for the eigenvalues that are simple in the limit, a multivariate Central Limit Theorem holds in all $d\ge2$ under centering by expected values. Unlike earlier work in $d=3$ by Figari, Orlandi and Teta and, independently, Ozawa from 1980s that was based on resolvent expansions, we rely on martingale representations and one-ball perturbation asymptotic controlled by methods of harmonic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Marek Biskup, Ryoki Fukushima

item.title: Spectral Theory of an Exactly Solvable Quantum-Optical Oscillator
item.dc:creator: Sam Johar, Joseph Kraisler

item.title: Algebraic Direct Sums and Generalized Drazin Invertibility
item.description: arXiv:2610.18433v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex Banach space $X$. We prove that the algebraic decomposition \[ X=\K(T)\oplus \Hq(T) \] forces both summands to be closed and hence characterizes generalized Drazin invertibility. This improves the classical characterizations of Mbekhta~\resultcite{Theorem~1.6}{MbekhtaKato}, Schmoeger~\resultcite{Theorem~4}{Schmoeger}, and Daji\'c and Koliha~\resultcite{Theorem~6.7}{DajicKoliha}, by removing their closedness assumptions. We also show that $T$ is generalized Drazin invertible if and only if \[ \dim\bigl(\K(T)\cap \Hq(T)\bigr)<\infty \quad\text{and}\quad \codim\bigl(\K(T)+\Hq(T)\bigr)<\infty. \] For ordinary Drazin invertibility, we obtain analogous finite-defect characterizations involving the hyperkernel and the hyperrange. We also give a characterization using pointwise nilpotence on an invariant summand. Finally, we consider arbitrary invariant algebraic decompositions and give a counterexample when the inverse of the restriction to one summand is not assumed bounded.
item.dc:creator: Zakariae Aznay, Fadil Chabbabi

item.title: Sign-indefinite transmission conditions and near-zero eigenvalues and resonances
item.description: arXiv:2610.18483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the linear operator for metamaterial modeling $$L_{c,d }=(\chi_{\RE^{3}\backslash\overline \Omega}+c)\nabla\!\cdot (\chi_{\RE^{3}\backslash\overline \Omega}+d)\nabla\,,$$ where the material parameters $c>0$ and $d$ are constant on each connected component of the bounded domain $\Omega$, $d$ is negative on at least one component of $\Omega$ and transmission boundary conditions hold at the interfaces. It turns out that $L_{c,d }$ has, as in the sign-definite case, an absolutely continuous spectrum equal to $[0,+\infty)$; however, contrary to the latter, it has a non-empty point spectrum; in particular, we find conditions on the parameters so that zero is a threshold eigenvalue. In the case $\Omega$ is connected, we study how such a threshold eigenvalue behaves under $\varepsilon$-small analytic perturbations of the parameters. We show that, depending on the position of the number $\frac12\,\frac{1+d(\ve)}{1-d(\ve)}$ relative to the nearest eigenvalue of the Neumann-Poincar\'e operator of the interface, the zero eigenvalue splits into two branches (analytic in $\varepsilon^{1/2}$), consisting either of two branches of resonances, or of one branch of negative eigenvalues and one of resonances.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Mantile, Andrea Posilicano

item.title: Generic boundary behavior of Dirichlet eigenfunctions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18619v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend Uhlenbeck's classical results on the generic properties of Laplacian eigenfunctions. In particular, we find a residual set of $C^k$ domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $k > n$, such that the nodal set of any Dirichlet eigenfunction intersects the boundary orthogonally along a $C^{k-1}$ embedded submanifold, whenever the intersection is non-empty. This is achieved by analyzing the boundary asymptotics of Dirichlet eigenfunctions via homogeneous harmonic polynomials and comparing their respective nodal sets. Along the way, we give a complete proof that generic Euclidean domains have simple Dirichlet eigenfunctions with zero as a regular value in the interior and zero as a regular value of the boundary normal derivative. In the special case of planar domains, a different argument provides one-parameter families of perturbed domains with the desired properties.
item.dc:creator: Alec Payne, Zihui Zhao

item.title: On the Kotani-Last Conjecture for the Dirac Operator
item.description: arXiv:2509.19072v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a dichotomy of almost periodicity for reflectionless one-dimensional Dirac operators whose spectra satisfy certain geometric conditions, extending work of Volberg--Yuditskii. We also construct a weakly mixing Dirac operator with a non-constant continuous potential whose spectrum is purely absolutely continuous, adapting Avila's argument for continuous Schr\"odinger operators. In particular, we disprove the Kotani--Last conjecture in the setting of one-dimensional Dirac operators.
item.dc:creator: Nyah Davis, \'iris Emilsd\'ottir, Long Li, Hangqi Liang

item.title: Bouncing-ball modes in ergodic billiards
item.description: arXiv:2609.36501v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that for a horizontally stretched Bunimovich billiard, for almost every stretching parameter, there exists a sequence of eigenfunctions concentrating in the rectangular part. Thanks to the work of Markarian--Oliffson Kamphorst--Pinto de Carvalho, we know that for an open set of parameters such billiards are ergodic. The proof is a result of interaction with ChatGPT 6: we were curious if it could establish the existence of bouncing ball modes for Bunimovich or Sinai billiards. That was not successful until we suggested varying the wings. That produced an essentially complete argument for the existence of quasimodes. We then suggested using Hassell's parameter-variation argument which led to the result about eigenfunctions. The argument was then significantly simplified and clarified by the authors.
item.dc:creator: Zhenhao Li, Maciej Zworski

item.title: Pointwise character bounds for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$
item.description: arXiv:2604.17589v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a basic pointwise bound for the irreducible characters of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ and, as an application, derive new $L^p$ bounds for these characters. Our approach is based on the descent of characters to singular sets and the cancellation in this formula.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 58 (2026), no. 10, Paper No. e70519, 24 pp
item.dc:creator: Yunfeng Zhang

item.title: Riccati Stability Without Auxiliary Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2609.06275v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the 2004 collection \emph{Unsolved Problems in Mathematical Systems and Control Theory}, Erik Verriest posed the problem of characterizing Riccati stability ``without invoking additional matrices.'' We give such a characterization through a scalar invariant of the resolvent family. The invariant is defined by covariance balances using at most $n^2+1$ frequency--direction pairs. A finite-dimensional separation argument shows that this covariance radius equals the optimal common ellipsoidal norm of the resolvent family. Combined with the strict bounded real lemma, this yields a necessary and sufficient condition for Riccati stability involving only the Hurwitz property of the first matrix and a single scalar inequality. The invariant reduces to the ordinary spectral radius for one matrix, lies between the pointwise spectral-radius and unscaled small-gain levels of the resolvent family, and coincides with the operator-space spectral radius of Shalit and Shamovich for the natural resolvent function space. The main results have been formally verified in the Lean proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Humpherys

item.title: Eigenvalue-Decomposition Cost Denoising for Predict-then-Optimize
item.description: arXiv:2609.15111v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Predict-then-optimize methods learn a mapping from features to unknown edge costs. They then solve the shortest-path problem on the predicted costs. We study a feature-free alternative for the case where the decision-maker observes many noisy cost vectors on a fixed network. The cost vectors are denoised by an eigenvalue decomposition (PCA) of their covariance matrix. Dijkstra's algorithm then runs on the result. We test this on the $5\times5$ grid of \citet{elmachtoub2022}, with $1000$ independent replications and a fresh ground truth in each. We compare against SPO+, against naive Dijkstra on noisy costs, and against two alternatives to a hand-picked rank $k$ (the Gavish-Donoho threshold and a Ledoit-Wolf filter). We also test a hybrid of SPO+ and PCA. Four findings emerge. First, the rank matters. Keeping $k=2$ components performs worse than no denoising. Second, when costs are close to linear in the features, the Gavish-Donoho threshold recovers the true rank without supervision. PCA-denoised Dijkstra outperforms SPO+ at $\deg=1$, but underperforms SPO+ at $\deg\geq 2$. The hybrid works best at $\deg=1$ and is slightly better than SPO+ at $\deg=2$. Third, when costs are strongly nonlinear ($\deg=4$), the signal is no longer low-rank, and only the Ledoit-Wolf filter clearly beats the naive baseline. Fourth, the benefit of denoising grows with network size on grids, but not on a layered non-grid network at high nonlinearity.
item.dc:creator: Henry Aldridge-Krawciw, Irene Aldridge

item.title: A sharp two-disk bound for the second positive Neumann eigenvalue under a curvature upper bound
item.description: arXiv:2609.26609v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the sharp two-disk comparison conjectured by Langford and Laugesen for the second positive Neumann eigenvalue under an upper Gaussian-curvature bound, and strengthen it to a shifted reciprocal inequality. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}$ be bounded, simply connected and Lipschitz, with $g=\omega|dz|^2$, where $\omega$ is continuous and positive on $\overline{\Omega}$ and $\Delta\log\omega+2K\omega\ge0$ in distributions. Write $A=|\Omega|_g$ and enumerate the spectrum by $0=\lambda_0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$. If $KA<4\pi$ when $K>0$, then $\frac{1}{\lambda_2}+\frac{1}{\lambda_3}>\frac{2}{\lambda_1(D_K(A/2))}$ and $\lambda_2<\lambda_1(D_K(A/2))$, where $D_K(A/2)$ is the constant-curvature disk of area $A/2$. The same conclusions hold for disk-type Lipschitz domains in smooth surfaces. In the subcritical regime, both bounds are sharp, as witnessed by an extremizing sequence of smooth connected domains of exact area and curvature whose Neumann eigenvalues converge, at every fixed index, to those of two disjoint equal model disks. At $KA=4\pi$ we obtain the sharp non-strict bounds $\lambda_2\le2K$ and $\lambda_2^{-1}+\lambda_3^{-1}\ge K^{-1}$. The proof combines two-pole Green coordinates, positive-kernel comparison, and simultaneous centering. We also establish a global quadratic deficit for the model area split.
item.dc:creator: Meiqi Liu, Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou

item.title: Reflectionless measures with singular continuous components on Widom sets
item.description: arXiv:2609.27133v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a detailed implementation of the mass-splitting construction of Nazarov, Volberg and Yuditskii for reflectionless measures with singular continuous components. The finite approximants are allowed to have isolated atoms. An exact local operation replaces each active atom by a short permanent interval and two child atoms, thereby eliminating the dependence of a future splitting scale on an already prescribed band width. Summable estimates for completed generations and fixed cylinders retain positive mass on a null Cantor set and exclude atoms in the limit. Uniform analytic estimates near the permanent intervals establish reflectionlessness and exclude endpoint singularities. A separate Green function estimate for thin pairs of intervals gives the Widom condition and regularity of the limiting compact set. The resulting probability measure has both a nonzero absolutely continuous component and a nonzero singular continuous component.
item.dc:creator: Long Li

item.title: Lower bounds for the magnitude of the minimum eigenvalue of graphs with applications to MaxCut and Chowla's cosine problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.01657v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Jin, Milojevi\'c, Tomon and Zhang established a powerful recursive estimate relating the positive eigenvalues of a graph whose least eigenvalue is small in absolute value. We establish a refinement of this result, yielding improved estimates across spectral graph theory and discrepancy theory, and for Chowla's cosine problem. Recent results of Janzer, Tomon and Yip allow us to directly transfer least eigenvalue estimates to the corresponding surplus estimates. Using these tools, we fully resolve a conjecture of R\"aty, Sudakov and Tomon. We show that, for an $n$-vertex graph $G$ with least eigenvalue $\lambda_n$ and surplus $\operatorname{sp}(G)$, if $G$ is $\epsilon$-far from all disjoint unions of cliques, then $|\lambda_n|\geq \Omega_\epsilon(n^{1/4})$ and $\operatorname{sp}(G)\geq \Omega_\epsilon(n^{5/4})$. Furthermore, we show that when $G$ is $n^{-o(1)}$-far from all disjoint unions of cliques, we have $|\lambda_n|\geq n^{1/4 - o(1)}$ and $\operatorname{sp}(G)\geq n^{5/4 - o(1)}$. Finally, we show that the surplus of a $K_t$-free graph with $m$ edges is at least $m^{0.614 - o(1)}$ as $m$ tends to infinity.
